steps.title: Touraine
steps.body: Touraine, around Tours, makes Vouvray and Montlouis from Chenin Blanc, dry to sweet and sparkling. Chinon, Bourgueil and Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil make Cabernet Franc reds, from light to structured. Touraine Sauvignon Blanc offers good value.

steps.title: The Central Vineyards
steps.body: Far upstream, the Central Vineyards are nearer Burgundy than the Atlantic. Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé make crisp, mineral Sauvignon Blanc. Sancerre's soils: terres blanches, Kimmeridgian marl, for full wines; caillottes, limestone pebbles, for fresh ones; silex, flint, for smoky wines. Sancerre also makes red and rosé from Pinot Noir.

steps.prompt: Match each wine to its grape.
steps.explanation: The Centre and Touraine use different grapes.

steps.title: Pouilly-Fumé and neighbours
steps.body: Pouilly-Fumé, on the opposite bank from Sancerre, is known for flint and a smoky, gunflint character. Menetou-Salon, Quincy, Reuilly and Coteaux du Giennois make similar Sauvignon at lower prices. Don't confuse Pouilly-Fumé with Pouilly-Fuissé, a Chardonnay from Burgundy's Mâconnais.

steps.prompt: Pouilly-Fumé and Pouilly-Fuissé are made from the same grape.
steps.explanation: Not true. Pouilly-Fumé is Loire Sauvignon Blanc; Pouilly-Fuissé is Burgundy Chardonnay.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Touraine makes Vouvray Chenin and Chinon Cabernet Franc
Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé make mineral Sauvignon
Soils like silex and caillottes shape Sancerre
